body.prompt: Late autumn in a traditional Korean hanok courtyard: curved dark-grey tiled roofs, a wooden maru porch, rows of brown earthenware jangdok jars along a stone wall, strings of dried red chili peppers. A tall old persimmon tree with bare twisting branches and only five glowing orange persimmons left at the very top. A little Korean girl about seven, with two short pigtails and a yellow quilted jacket, stands on tiptoe reaching up with a long bamboo pole toward the last persimmons. Behind her, an elderly Korean grandmother with white hair in a low bun, a quilted plum vest and a long grey skirt, gently rests her wrinkled hand on the pole, smiling warmly. Golden late-afternoon light, a few orange leaves falling.
